review_candidates.title: Head of Financial Planning & Analysis
review_candidates.description: MSF is an international, independent medical humanitarian organization. We are a non-profit, self-governed worldwide movement of more than 63,000 people. We provide emergency medical assistance during armed conflict, natural disasters, outbreaks of deadly diseases and assist those who are excluded from healthcare. MSF delivers care based on need and when we see injustice, we speak out. We are an organization that remains impartial, knowledgeable, and effective, and this is what makes the difference between life and death. People are our priority. At Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)/ Artsen zonder Grenzen, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We encourage diverse applicants including individuals of all gender identities, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, social and marital status, people with different abilities and all other diversity characteristics and how they intersect. With immediate effect, our Finance department is looking for a: Head of Financial Planning & Analysis (40 h/w) Based in Amsterdam Médecins Sans Frontières Operational Centre Amsterdam (MSF OCA) is undergoing a significant reorganisation of its Finance Department. Historically organised along a split between Programs and Headquarters, Finance is moving towards an integrated, global functional model designed to better support MSF OCA’s strategic direction. This new model brings together expertise across geographies and teams and is structured around three core functions: Global Accounting Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) Innovation and Learning The aim of this reorganisation is to strengthen consistency, accountability, and quality while enabling Finance to operate as one global function, working seamlessly across headquarters and country-level operations. As part of this transformation, we are recruiting a Head of Financial Planning & Analysis to lead the FP&A function across headquarters and country programs. You will report to the Director of Finance and Business Operations, sit on the Finance Management Team, and lead a team of experienced advisors and specialists. Why This Role Matters This role brings together people with very different perspectives and areas of expertise: colleagues supporting country programs and emergencies, headquarters teams and funding partnerships. The Head of FP&A will lead 13 positions across the Operational Finance, Headquarters Finance and Funding Coordination teams, creating the conditions for them to work as one function while valuing the distinct contribution each team makes. It is an opportunity to build stronger connections across Finance and ensure this diversity of experience translates into better support for the organisation. The ambition is to move beyond reviewing budgets and reporting results after the fact. FP&A will work alongside leaders in headquarters and country programs to understand their portfolios, anticipate financial and operational risks, and help them make better decisions earlier. As an internal control partner, Finance will not take over ownership of risks and controls. Instead, it will bring structure, challenge and practical support: helping teams assess where controls are weak, agree proportionate improvements and follow through on them. The result should be stronger control maturity, fewer recurring audit findings and a Finance function that is closer to the work, more useful in emergencies and more influential in shaping OCA’s direction. Objective As Head of Financial Planning & Analysis, you will: Define and drive the FP&A strategy, translating OCA’s strategic direction into coherent multi-year plans, budgets, forecasts and performance insight. Lead the Finance and Budget component of OCA’s business planning cycle, including annual budgeting, multi-year forecasting and clear recommendations to the Management Team and other governance bodies. Bring business partnering to life across headquarters and country programs, ensuring senior leaders and Operations receive practical, timely and decision-focused financial advice. Develop Finance’s role as a portfolio controller and internal control partner, supporting control assessments, stronger risk awareness and action to reduce recurring audit findings. Make Finance more emergency-ready by developing an approach that supports rapid operational decisions and by maintaining a strong partnership with the Emergency Support Department. Provide high-quality financial analysis, scenario planning and advice on budget integrity, cash and liquidity, foreign exchange exposure, restricted funding and donor requirements. Strengthen funding coordination by connecting fundraising, Operations and Finance, aligning funding with operational priorities, and developing the function internationally with other Operational Directorates. Engage in OCA’s strategic planning processes and represent FP&A on relevant internal, international and Audit & Risk Committee platforms. Set direction for and develop a team of senior, independent advisors and specialists, creating a collaborative culture with clear priorities, accountability and room for professional judgement. Contribute as a member of the Finance Management Team and help lead the wider department. What We’re Looking For You are a relationship-centred finance leader who enjoys working beyond the boundaries of Finance. You listen well, understand operational needs and turn financial information into advice that people can act on. You combine strategic thinking with delivery. You can set a compelling direction for FP&A, lead a complex planning cycle and present forecasts, risks and choices with confidence. You understand the realities of medical humanitarian operations and can adapt financial planning and controls to fast-moving, uncertain and emergency contexts. You are comfortable leading experienced, independent professionals. You create clarity, build trust and hold people accountable without crowding out their expertise. You bring energy and judgement to organisational change, helping people move from a new structure on paper to a stronger way of working in practice. Candidate Profile Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics or a related field. At least nine years of relevant finance experience, including experience in a senior management role. Substantial experience with financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, performance management and decision support in a complex international organisation. Previous MSF experience is desirable. Experience gained in OCA or another MSF operational centre or entity is very welcome and experience in a related or similar role with another global INGO will also be considered. Country-program management experience is desirable, either gained in Finance directly or in another Country Management Team position. Demonstrated experience of business partnering with senior operational stakeholders and leading teams through change. Strong understanding of financial risk, internal controls, donor requirements and the humanitarian operating environment. Fluency in English is required; other languages are an asset. Willingness to travel occasionally to MSF country programs and international meetings. This is an opportunity to shape how Finance supports decisions across OCA at a pivotal moment of change. You will build a more connected and forward-looking FP&A function, strengthen financial stewardship and help ensure that resources are directed where they can best support medical humanitarian action. To foster a healthy work-life balance we have a remote working policy where you can work 40% of your weekly hours from home, 60% working in person in the office. Coming together at our office in Amsterdam allows us to have informal exchanges and chance encounters, share ideas more freely and solve challenges together in real-time. We Offer An opportunity to lead a newly integrated FP&A function and shape Finance within a major international medical humanitarian organisation. A Dutch employment contract (40 hours/week), with a preferred start date of 1 December 2026 . A management contract for 3 years with option for renewal, subject to satisfactory performance, with another 3 years (maximum 6 years in total). Gross monthly salary between €5,922 and €8,153 (full-time), depending on experience. An environment that fosters diversity, with colleagues from around the world representing various cultures and backgrounds. Other benefits include: 30 days off (based on a full-time employment) A competitive pension scheme 8% holiday allowance, paid out with the salary in May Commuting allowance (terms and conditions apply) & work from home allowance L&D will support you with a variety of learning and development opportunities with internal and external trainings and courses Application Do you recognise yourself in this profile? We welcome you to apply directly via our website. Please upload your letter of motivation and Curriculum Vitae in English as one combined document. The closing date for applications is: 30 September 2026 . Selection will be by means of two interviewing rounds, including an assessment/case study. A certificate of good conduct/VOG is needed should you be selected for the role. First-round interviews: from week of 5 October 2026. Please note the application deadline specified above may be subject to change at MSF-Netherland’s discretion. Information For questions about the role or process, contact Irene Tellekamp (Team Recruitment) at irene.tellekamp@amsterdam.msf.org . ***No agencies please***

review_candidates.title: Global Head of Lifecycle Marketing
review_candidates.description: About The Company Scrambly is one of the fastest-growing adtech startups in the world, featured in the AppsFlyer Performance Index and Singular ROI Index in just 3.5 years. We’re growing 250%+ YoY across revenue, team, product, and technology — fully bootstrapped and profitable. We’re building the future of app discovery: a reward-powered alternative to the App Store and Google Play. Our loyalty-driven ecosystem connects millions of users with the world’s top apps and delivers unmatched, ROI-focused growth for mobile advertisers. Our mission is to build a true alternative to traditional app stores — fueled by rewards and data — and create a new, performance-first growth engine for mobile app advertisers. About The Role We’re looking for a Global Head of Lifecycle Marketing to own retention, CRM, lifecycle communications and LiveOps across all of our apps and geos. You’ll take a large, fast-moving campaign estate — dozens of in-app messages, emails and push notifications per app — and turn it into a clean, measured, always-on machine. The headline goal: grow LiveOps revenue several-fold into 7-figure-monthly territory within a year, while making every campaign attributable and incremental. This isn’t a seat-warmer role. You’ll live in Mixpanel and Customer.io, run a relentless testing program, kill what doesn’t move the numbers, and lean hard on AI — MCP/Claude workflows, automation inside Customer.io, and predictive models that recommend the next best message per user. You’ll be fully hands-on and build a team as you scale. If you’re a super-energetic, data-driven growth hacker who wants full ownership of a lifecycle engine and hates waste, this is your seat. What You’ll Do Own the whole lifecycle engine — retention, CRM, lifecycle comms, and LiveOps across every app and every geo, and build a team around it (US, UK, CA, FR). Scale LiveOps revenue several-fold into 7-figure-monthly territory within your first year, all incremental and attributable. Map and clean the campaign estate — measure the incrementality of every campaign across upper, mid, and deep funnel, re-engagement, retargeting, affiliate and lifecycle comms, and kill or replace whatever isn’t pulling its weight. Run a relentless testing program — build up to 15+ A/B tests a week, plus 3 new retargeting tests a week, starting with the lowest-hanging-fruit segments. Build LiveOps into an evergreen engine — a standing calendar of events across weekdays and weekends, refreshed continuously, plus a steady drumbeat of internal reactivation tests. Live in the data — Mixpanel cohorts, funnels and retention curves; hold aggressive incremental targets and report clean readouts by app, geo and cohort. Make it AI-native — use MCP/Claude and AI automation inside Customer.io to build, segment, personalise and QA at scale, with predictive models recommending the next best communication per user. Work like an owner — treat the revenue number like your own money; see the gap, close it, no hand-holding. Streamline CRM with Product — set specific lifecycle goals every quarter and build a repeatable, data-driven cadence with the product team. Build and lead the team — hire as you scale and grow a full retention/lifecycle/LiveOps function, staying hands-on as a player-coach. What You Bring 7+ years in lifecycle / CRM / retention marketing for consumer apps, including leading a team. Proven scale — you’ve run lifecycle at consumer apps with millions of users across multiple geos, orchestrating dozens of concurrent campaigns. A track record of driving 7-figure monthly revenue or engagement through lifecycle, retention and LiveOps — with the numbers to prove it. All three channels — in-app messages, email and push notifications, at real volume. Deep CRM/messaging platform skills — we use Customer.io; Braze or similar is fine. Advanced product-analytics chops — we use Mixpanel; Amplitude or similar is fine. Self-serve, no waiting on anyone for a number. Fluency in the economics — incrementality, cost tracking, performance tracking, A/B test design, LTV and retention/engagement cohorts. Advanced AI user — MCP/Claude workflows, AI automation and predictive user-behaviour modelling are part of how you work. Owner mentality — you fix problems and move without being managed; results over activity, every time. Relentless energy and standards — a 10/10 operator who goes beyond the brief and is restless with “good enough.” English C1+ — you work fluently across US, UK, CA and FR markets. Experience We’re Looking For You likely have 7+ years of scaling lifecycle and retention across multiple consumer apps with millions of users, where lifecycle was a core revenue driver — not an afterthought. You’ve owned the number, run the tests, and built the automation. Industries You Likely Come From Mobile gaming and gaming-adjacent apps with strong LiveOps. Consumer subscription and freemium apps (health, fitness, education, media, dating). Rewards, cashback, loyalty, and “earn” apps. Fintech and neobank consumer apps with heavy lifecycle engagement. E-commerce/marketplace apps with sophisticated CRM. Types Of Companies You May Have Worked At High-growth consumer app scale-ups where retention drives the P&L. Mobile-first companies with mature LiveOps and lifecycle programs. Data- and AI-forward growth teams that test relentlessly. Companies operating across multiple countries and app portfolios. How We Work Meritocratic, fast, product-first, and flat. We hold an explicit A-player bar and value direct, honest feedback over titles or seniority. You’ll have full autonomy from day one — and full accountability for the outcome. Opinions start the conversation; numbers end it. The bar: grow LiveOps into 7-figure-monthly revenue within a year, running 15+ tests a week across a clean, AI-driven lifecycle engine — every campaign incremental and attributable. If that lights you up, let’s talk. By submitting this application, I agree that my personal data will be collected, processed, and retained by the company solely for the purposes of managing and assessing my candidacy.
